citations.quote: Let $\pi$ be a probability on a finite product state space and let $K_B$ be a supplied proper full conditional kernel for a nonempty block $B$. The exact block-update kernel $P_B$ of [[alg-gibbs-block-update]] is reversible with respect to $\pi$ and leaves $\pi$ invariant.

**Inputs:** A common finite-product measurable state space $(S,\mathcal S)$ with target probability $\pi$, an integer $m\ge1$, and for each $j=1,\ldots,m$ a nonempty block $B_j$ with its supplied proper full conditional kernel for $\pi$. Invoke [[alg-gibbs-block-update]] for each block to obtain its exact update kernel $P_j:S\to S$. Select random scan, systematic scan, or both; if random scan is selected, also supply fixed weights $w_j\ge0$ with $\sum_{j=1}^m w_j=1$.

**Admissible conditions:** Every $P_j$ acts on this same $(S,\mathcal S)$ and is an exact block-update kernel for this same target $\pi$. The weights are required only for the random-scan branch; systematic scan takes no weights.

**Outputs:** For each selected mode, its one-update random-scan kernel $P_{\rm rand}:S\to S$ or full-sweep systematic kernel $P_{\rm sweep}:S\to S$; for systematic scan, also the phase-indexed single-update kernels $P_1,\ldots,P_m$.

**Random-scan instructions:** At each update, independently draw $j\in\{1,\ldots,m\}$ with probabilities $w_1,\ldots,w_m$ and apply $P_j$ to the current state. The one-update kernel is
$$P_{\rm rand}(x,A)=\sum_{j=1}^m w_jP_j(x,A).$$
Uniform random scan is the special case $w_j=1/m$.

**Systematic-scan instructions:** Starting from the current state, apply $P_1$, then $P_2$, through $P_m$ in that fixed order; repeat the same order for each subsequent sweep. For kernels, $P_1\cdots P_m$ means chronological composition: apply $P_1$ first and $P_m$ last, as in [[def-composition-of-probability-kernels]]. Return the full-sweep kernel $P_{\rm sweep}=P_1\cdots P_m$. Observing after each single update gives the phase-indexed sequence $P_1,\ldots,P_m,P_1,\ldots$ and is generally time-inhomogeneous; observing only at full-sweep boundaries gives a homogeneous chain with kernel $P_{\rm sweep}$. The scan kernels are well-defined by [[lem-gibbs-scan-schemes-are-probability-kernels]].

For probability kernels $K:(S,\Sigma)\to(T,\Tau)$ and $L:(T,\Tau)\to(U,\Upsilon)$, their **composition**, in the order K then L, is
$$(KL)(s,A)=\int_T L(t,A)\,K(s,dt),\qquad s\in S,\quad A\in\Upsilon.$$

The kernel convention is [[def-measure-kernel-and-probability-kernel]]. The integrand is measurable in t and lies in $[0,1]$, so the displayed number exists in $[0,1]$. As a function of s it is measurable by [[thm-measurability-of-integration-against-a-kernel]], applied to the product-measurable function $(s,t)\mapsto L(t,A)$: its threshold preimages are rectangles $S\times\{t:L(t,A)>a\}$. The probability-kernel assertion and associativity are justified by [[lem-kernel-composition-is-well-defined-and-associative]].

Composition refers to specified pointwise kernels. Almost-everywhere classes alone do not define this formula until representatives and the relevant measures are specified. For an empty source the candidate is the empty map. No choice of versions or assumption of AC enters this definition.

The composition KL of probability kernels $K:S\to T$ and $L:T\to U$ is a probability kernel $S\to U$. If $M:U\to V$ is another probability kernel, then $(KL)M=K(LM)$ at every source point and every measurable subset of V. Equality concerns the specified kernels, not unspecified almost-everywhere classes.

Let $K$ be a probability kernel on a measurable space $(E,\mathcal E)$
([[def-measure-kernel-and-probability-kernel]]), and let $\pi$ be a
probability measure on $(E,\mathcal E)$ ([[def-probability-measure]]). The
probability measure $\pi$ is **invariant** for $K$, and $\pi$ is a
**stationary distribution** of $K$, when

$$(\pi K)(A):=\int_E K(x,A)\,\pi(dx)=\pi(A)\qquad\text{for every }A\in\mathcal E .$$

The set function $\pi K$ is again a probability measure: for fixed $A$ the map
$x\mapsto K(x,A)$ is measurable and lies in $[0,1]$, so the integral exists in
$[0,1]$; for pairwise disjoint $A_n\in\mathcal E$ the identity
$K(x,\bigcup_nA_n)=\sum_nK(x,A_n)$ of the measure $K(x,\cdot)$ and the
monotone convergence theorem for nonnegative functions
([[thm-monotone-convergence-for-the-integral]]) give
$\sigma$-additivity of $\pi K$; and $K(x,E)=1$ for every $x$ gives
$(\pi K)(E)=1$. Thus $(\pi K)(A)=\pi(A)$ is an identity between two probability
measures evaluated at $A$.

A $K$-chain whose initial law is $\pi$ is called **stationary** when
$\pi K=\pi$. Stationarity of the process is a statement about all of its
finite-dimensional laws and is proved, not assumed, from $\pi K=\pi$; see
[[thm-invariant-initial-law-makes-the-chain-stationary]].

On a countable state space $E$ with sigma-algebra $2^E$ and transition matrix
$p(x,y)=K(x,\{y\})$ ([[def-transition-matrix-and-n-step-transition-probabilities]]),
a measure on $E$ is its weighted sum of Dirac masses at singletons
([[thm-measures-on-countable-discrete-spaces-are-weighted-dirac-sums]]), so
invariance is equivalent to the matrix identity

$$\pi(y)=\sum_{x\in E}\pi(x)\,p(x,y)\qquad\text{for every }y\in E .$$

The definition fixes no irreducibility, aperiodicity or uniqueness hypothesis,
and it selects no conditional-expectation versions; the display defines a
single measure $\pi K$ and asserts an identity for it. A transient, periodic or
reducible chain may have several invariant probability measures or none.

Let $(\Theta,\mathcal T)$ and $(\mathcal X,\mathcal A)$ be measurable spaces,
let $\pi$ be a probability measure on $(\Theta,\mathcal T)$, and let
$K:\Theta\times\mathcal A\to[0,1]$ be a probability kernel. For
$C\in\mathcal T\otimes\mathcal A$, write
$C_\theta=\{x\in\mathcal X:(\theta,x)\in C\}$ and set
$$J(C)=\int_\Theta K(\theta,C_\theta)\,\pi(d\theta).$$
Then $J$ is a probability measure on the product sigma-algebra, and for every
nonnegative product-measurable $h$,
$$\int_{\Theta\times\mathcal X}h(\theta,x)\,J(d\theta,dx)=\int_\Theta\left(\int_\mathcal Xh(\theta,x)\,K(\theta,dx)\right)\pi(d\theta).$$
In particular, $J(A\times B)=\int_AK(\theta,B)\,\pi(d\theta)$ for
$A\in\mathcal T$ and $B\in\mathcal A$.

Let $I$ be a finite nonempty index set, let $(S_i,\mathcal S_i)_{i\in I}$ be measurable spaces, set $S=\prod_{i\in I}S_i$ with its finite product sigma-algebra, and let $\pi$ be a probability measure on $S$. For a nonempty block $B\subseteq I$, write $S_B=\prod_{i\in B}S_i$, $S_{-B}=\prod_{i\in I\setminus B}S_i$, let $p_{-B}:S\to S_{-B}$ be the coordinate projection, and define $\pi_{-B}(D):=\pi(p_{-B}^{-1}(D))$ for measurable $D\subseteq S_{-B}$.

Products and product sigma-algebras use the empty-product convention in [[def-product-sigma-algebra-and-finite-product-sigma-algebras]]: if $B=I$, then $S_{-B}$ is the one-point space $\{()\}$ with its trivial sigma-algebra.

A **proper full conditional kernel** for block $B$ is a supplied probability kernel $K_B:S_{-B}\to S_B$ such that for every product-measurable $C\subseteq S$ and every measurable $D\subseteq S_{-B}$,
$$
\pi\bigl(C\cap p_{-B}^{-1}(D)\bigr)=\int_D K_B(z,C_z)\,\pi_{-B}(dz),\qquad C_z:=\{u\in S_B:\operatorname{splice}_B(z,u)\in C\}.
$$
Here $\operatorname{splice}_B(z,u)$ is the unique state whose coordinates on $I\setminus B$ are $z$ and whose coordinates on $B$ are $u$. This is the event-identity definition of a regular conditional distribution of the block given the retained coordinates, with every kernel section a probability measure at every $z$. It makes no existence claim; the A-page density corollary gives one sufficient case.

**Inputs:** The finite product state space and target law from [[def-gibbs-full-conditional-kernel]], a nonempty block $B$, its supplied proper full conditional kernel $K_B$, and a current state $x\in S$.

**Output:** A new state $x'\in S$ whose retained coordinates equal $x_{-B}$ and whose updated block is sampled from $K_B(x_{-B},\cdot)$.

The transition kernel is
$$P_B(x,C)=\int_{S_B}\mathbf1_C\!\left(\operatorname{splice}_B(x_{-B},u)\right)K_B(x_{-B},du),\qquad C\in\mathcal S.$$
Operationally, retain every coordinate outside $B$, draw $u$ from the full conditional kernel at the retained value, and replace the coordinates in $B$ by $u$. The finite product sigma-algebra makes the splice map measurable; the kernel-integral theorem makes the displayed evaluation measurable in $x$. The well-definedness result is [[lem-gibbs-block-update-is-a-probability-kernel]].

Let $P$ be a probability kernel on $(S,\mathcal S)$ and let $\pi$ be a probability measure on that space. The kernel $P$ is **reversible with respect to $\pi$**, or satisfies **detailed balance**, when
$$
\int_A P(x,C)\,\pi(dx)=\int_C P(y,A)\,\pi(dy)\qquad(A,C\in\mathcal S).
$$
This is the symmetry of the two-time transition flow $\pi(dx)P(x,dy)$, stated through its values on measurable rectangles. The definition is for a general measurable state space and makes no irreducibility, uniqueness, or convergence assertion. Invariance means $\int P(x,A)\,\pi(dx)=\pi(A)$ for every $A\in\mathcal S$, as in [[def-invariant-and-stationary-distribution-for-a-markov-kernel]].

derivations.claim: For two probability kernels $P,Q$, the iterated-kernel identity [F5] gives $\int (PQ)(x,A)\,\pi(dx)=\int Q(y,A)\,(\pi P)(dy)$.
To prove that reversibility can fail, give $S=\{0,1\}^2$ its full sigma-algebra and target masses $\pi(0,0)=\pi(0,1)=\pi(1,0)=1/5$ and $\pi(1,1)=2/5$.
Let $P_X$ refresh $X$ and $P_Y$ refresh $Y$, using the kernels in step 3.1, and set $P=P_XP_Y$ in chronological order.

boundaries.evidence: Statement assumes m≥1 and a target probability, so its list and state space are nonempty.
Step 3.1 uses strictly positive finite target masses; the invariance argument in steps 1.1–2.1 remains valid for arbitrary target probability masses, including zeros.
Statement permits m=1, where step 2.1 reduces to invariance of one update; the existence witness uses m=2.
Step 2.1 applies also to a degenerate target when proper full-conditionals are supplied.
Statement imposes no continuous endpoint parameter; step 3.1 explicitly enumerates all finite conditioning values.
Steps 3.1–3.2 specify every witness probability explicitly, with no choice axiom.
